## M4 to the certification review {#m4}

| step | work | done when | needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| proofs | transport monotonicity in the normalised temperature gradients, by a structural certificate and by derivative bounds with input splitting | a certificate per model, both routes agreeing | — |
| output bounds | certified output bounds per ensemble member over each training box: transport, EC per launcher family, pedestal around the ITER states the loop visits | certificates; transport bounds wired into the guard | — |
| calibration | split-conformal intervals at the agreed coverage, fitted on validation splits and reported on test splits; not applicable to the pedestal model, which has no labelled data | coverage table, intervals stored with the model hash | — |
| robustness | local robustness on small boxes around loop states | proved, falsified (with counterexample) or timed out, per surrogate | a CPU node if the proofs are heavy |
| EC closed loop | about 20 states per launcher from coupled runs, compared with GENRAY on the same launches | comparison table, pass or fail | one small batch job |
| guards | guards read the certified boxes and bounds; fallback rates checked against a threshold | rates reported against the threshold | owner: the threshold |
| reports and CI | one verification report per surrogate, stating MAST-U's limitation; CI re-proves the cheap properties when a surrogate changes | reports cite their certificates; CI passes in both test modes | — |
| review | the M4 report and the certification review | the owner's review recorded | owner (the gate) |

Bounds over 17- and 68-dimensional input boxes may be loose. The tightness reached is
reported, and the boxes are not shrunk to make bounds tighter.

## JOREK: finish J5, then decide its role {#jorek}

1. Analyse the second case (b) job. The fit window for case (b) is fixed before looking at
   that job: 4 to 10 decades above each run's minimum energy, with the same agreement checks,
   and location from the flow perturbation. An n that has not grown 6 decades by the end is
   reported as "no measurable growth", not as stable.
2. The time-step check: restart each growing pedestal mode from the same snapshot at Δt = 1
   and Δt = 0.5, and compare over matching windows.
3. The grid check needs an owner decision. Repeating the slow emergence on the doubled grid
   costs far more than the remaining jobs. The options are a grid check on case (a)'s two fast
   pedestal modes instead, a long chain of case (b) jobs, a JOREK patch to carry an eigenmode
   across grids, or the time-step check alone.
4. Report the case (b) growth rates per n with their convergence status, and add a ceiling if
   the grid check stays open.
5. The owner then decides what JOREK becomes in the toolkit: a surrogate of a JOREK quantity,
   reference runs only, or neither. One case (b) n-scan costs about two six-hour node-jobs
   before any convergence check, which bears on that choice.

## Decisions ahead {#decisions-ahead}

| when | decision |

| end of M4 | the certification review |

## After M4: M5 inputs {#m5}

M5 propagates uncertainty through the coupled simulation and validates it, ending in a
physicist sign-off. Inputs to ask for at the M4 review: a Tier A validation set (experimental
shot data are out of scope), the uncertain inputs and their priors, the quantity of
interest, and how the discrepancy budget is split across transport, sources, pedestal and
equilibrium. The certified boxes and conformal intervals from M4 become M5's trust regions
and surrogate-error terms.

the final monotone surrogate and QLKNN using matched scenario, grid and solver settings.
Record compilation separately from execution, resource allocation, finite profiles, solver
status, profile errors and accepted-state guard rejection. Every output carries provenance.

Jacobian construction. Keep unresolved overlap visible ([K-022](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-022)). Historical speed-up belongs
to the original model; timings from different hosts or drivers cannot establish final-model

with allocation and solver settings stated.

## Train and integrate the response surrogates {#responses}

Define physically related case groups and label a small baseline. Keep entire groups together
in training and holdout sets. Inspect failed labels, sampled domains and physical integrals.
After the baseline, agree held-out accuracy metrics and targets with the owner.

Train structured EC ensembles and evaluate untouched holdouts. The selected pretrained
ITER pedestal is ported directly; no second network needs to learn its outputs. Integrate source and boundary
responses into TORAX behind guards with Tier A fallbacks. Supply channel adapters required
by the selected targets. Check gradients, finite execution, energy/particle balance, physical
rejection, fallback use and coupled cost. Pointwise profile errors alone do not establish
absorbed-power accuracy.

**Done when:** the reference datasets, checkpoints, accuracy results, guarded coupled checks
and matched cost measurements have provenance and meet the agreed criteria.

EC dataset v1 is labelled ([3120 of 3120 cases produce readable output (20 of 20 check cases); median 84.8 s of GENRAY time per case]{.claim}[C-164](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-164){.cid .st-measured}). The first baseline learns the totals but its
pointwise profile model does not beat the training mean ([driven current RMSE 3.30 kA/MW against 13.5 kA/MW for the training mean; pointwise profile model: current-density RMSE 2.20e4 A/m^2 against 2.09e4 A/m^2 for the mean]{.claim}[C-166](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-166){.cid .st-measured}), so the EC model
needs a structured profile output. [K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028) records that every case uses one equilibrium.
The owner then set the targets and restricted the states ([K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028) option b); the structured
surrogate meets all three targets ([all three targets pass: absorbed power 0.01% and driven current 2.7% median relative error (targets 10%), heating centre 0.0036 median absolute error in rho (target 0.05)]{.claim}[C-168](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-168){.cid .st-measured},
[entry 38](log/38-structured-ec-surrogate.qmd)). Both the EC surrogate and the ITER pedestal
now run inside TORAX behind their guards ([runs under jit for both launchers with the surrogate serving the source; energy balance within 1e-6 and particles within 1e-10; derivatives through Newton match finite differences to 1e-7]{.claim}[C-171](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-171){.cid .st-tested}, [runs under jit with EPEDNN setting the pedestal; energy balance within 1e-6 and particles within 1e-10; derivatives through Newton match finite differences to 1e-7]{.claim}[C-173](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-173){.cid .st-tested},

## Close M3, then start M4 {#verification}

Audit the complete M3 criteria: held-out accuracy, differentiable guarded execution and
measured end-to-end speed-up. Transport accuracy alone does not close the RF/pedestal tasks.
Keep the ion-flux convention, monotonicity departure, default-root tolerance and domain limits
visible ([K-024](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-024), [K-025](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-025), [K-026](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-026)).

After M3 acceptance, agree verification properties and trajectory tolerances with the owner.
Prove properties over declared input boxes, calibrate uncertainty on held-out data, compare
trajectories against Tier A references and prepare per-surrogate verified-domain reports.
Certification review closes M4. Sampled monotonicity and raw ensemble spread are not
certificates.
